evidence.quote: A 41-year-old unmarried woman with a four-year history of a polymyomatous uterus and endometriosis presented with AUB.

She had previously been treated for iron-deficiency anemia with oral iron therapy, which was discontinued, and she did not receive adequate follow-up, having been lost to follow-up for the past three years.

summary.text: A 41-year-old unmarried North African woman with a four-year history of uterine fibroids and endometriosis, previously treated for iron-deficiency anemia and lost to follow-up for three years, presented with profuse abnormal uterine bleeding and impaired consciousness.

On admission she was hemodynamically unstable and confused with Glasgow Coma Scale 10/15, tachypnea, tachycardia, pallor and a first measurable blood pressure of 55/30 mmHg, with hemoglobin 1.4 g/dL, hematocrit 5.1%, INR 3.43, pH 6.88 and lactate 6.32 mmol/L.

Pelvic ultrasound showed an enlarged uterus with a FIGO type 2-5 fibroid measuring 4.6 × 4.6 cm and a FIGO type 6 pedunculated fibroid measuring 4.8 × 4.7 cm, with a small volume of intra-abdominal fluid.

After norepinephrine stabilization and rapid sequence induction she underwent total hysterectomy via midline laparotomy with 6 units of packed red blood cells, 5 units of fresh frozen plasma, tranexamic acid and cefazolin; estimated blood loss was 400 mL.
At 10 hours postoperatively hemoglobin was 6.8 g/dL and norepinephrine was weaned off within the first few hours; two more units of packed red blood cells were given on postoperative Day 1.
About 23 hours postoperatively she developed acute respiratory distress diagnosed as cardiogenic pulmonary edema with LVEF 28% and a restrictive mitral inflow pattern, with ARDS and TRALI excluded.

Treatment with furosemide, fluid restriction, oxygen, bisoprolol, ramipril and spironolactone without inotropes led to oxygen weaning on Day 4, pulmonary edema resolution by Day 7, discharge on Day 10, and LVEF 50% with complete cardiac recovery at one month.

evidence.quote: a platelet count of 98,000/µL (mildly decreased)

ambiguities.issue: The narrative gives the admission platelet count as 98,000/µL while Table 1 prints 98 (and 149, 118, 120 later) under a /µL row label with a 150,000-400,000 reference range, so the table values are on a different scale (probably thousands).
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not rescale the table cells or assume their units.

evidence.quote: 1.32 on Day 1

ambiguities.issue: INR on Day 1 is 1.32 in the coagulopathy discussion but 1.36 in Table 1 and in the diagnostic workup paragraph; both values are kept review_only.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign the 1.8 g/L value to 10 hours postoperatively.
